M5 Slice 4 — hide/unhide (§6.8). 23 files, all full files at repo-relative paths. Extracts at the repo root:

bash

Files to DELETE: none
Nothing renamed, nothing superseded. No migration, no packages, no schema change, Program.cs untouched.

New (11)
Orders/OrderVisibility.cs (the two writes), Orders/OrderHistoryReads.cs (guest history, filtered hidden list, visibility log), Orders/OrderVisibilityWorkflow.cs (the §9 broadcast shell), Pages/Table/TableHistory.razor at /table/history, Pages/Administration/HiddenRecords.razor at /administration/hidden-records, three test files, and docs/_append/BUILD_PROGRESS-m5-slice-4.md. Plus _CHANGES.md.

Edited (12)
OrderEventVocabulary.cs (+2 consts), SittingRecordReads.cs (+GetOrderRecordAsync, three statements templated by one const WHERE fragment — the sitting-scoped SQL is character-identical after substitution), RestaurantTime.cs (+StartOfDay/StartOfNextDay), OrdersServiceCollectionExtensions.cs, Home.razor, TableArea.razor, TableOrderSurface.razor (one <a>), the four Administration*.razor header strips (one <a> each), OrderTestWorld.cs, OrdersWiringTests.cs.

Every edited file was extracted byte-exact from dump.txt (SHA-256 verified against the dump's own metadata) and then patched, so git diff will show only the intended lines — 1 line each on the four admin pages, 2 on TableOrderSurface.

Verification I could do without a compiler
Brace/paren/bracket balance on all C# (string-literal- and raw-string-aware), the same on both @code blocks, HTML tag balance and Razor markup brace balance on both new pages, no tabs/CRs/trailing whitespace. Long lines are all XML-doc <param> tags, matching the 203-char precedent already in SittingRecordReads.cs.

Three things worth knowing before you build
@formname is a literal in both new forms ("hide-order", "unhide-order"), matching 15 of the 17 existing usages. I'd originally used a const via @formname="@Const" and backed it out — Passkeys.razor is the only dynamic precedent and it uses the explicit @(…) form, so a literal removes the question entirely.
ListOrderRecordsForSittingAsync is now an expression-bodied async method. Legal, and the one shape here with no precedent in the tree.
No local declared inside a markup @foreach — nothing else in the tree does that, so IsExpanded(summary) and CountSentence(count) are methods.
Expected test delta: +37 facts → 877 total, 862 passing, 15 still skipped. Two of those skips (Guest_HidesClosedOrder_AdminCanUnhide in particular) are finally writable at M6.

What's left in M5: the cross-cutting event explorer. All three engines exist — ISittingRecordReads, IMenuEventLog, ISecurityEventLog — and what's missing is one screen over them with a shared filter.
